slides.title: Why NumPy? 🧮
slides.content:
# The Core of Data Science

NumPy (Numerical Python) provides the `ndarray` object, which is up to 50x faster than traditional Python lists.

## Creating Arrays
```python
import numpy as np

# From list
arr = np.array([1, 2, 3])

# Zeros and Ones
z = np.zeros((3, 3)) # 3x3 matrix of 0s
o = np.ones((2, 2))  # 2x2 matrix of 1s

# Range
r = np.arange(0, 10, 2) # [0, 2, 4, 6, 8]
```

slides.title: Array Operations
slides.content:
# Vectorization ⚡

No loops needed! Operations apply element-wise.

```python
import numpy as np

a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
b = np.array([10, 20, 30])

print(a + b) # [11, 22, 33]
print(a * 2) # [2, 4, 6]
print(a > 2) # [False, False, True]
```

## Universal Functions (ufuncs)
Fast math functions.
```python
import numpy as np

np.sqrt(a)
np.log(a)
np.mean(a)
```

slides.title: Indexing and Slicing
slides.content:
# Advanced Access 🕵️

## Slicing 2D Arrays
`arr[row, col]`
```python
mat = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])

# Get row 0
print(mat[0, :]) # [1, 2]

# Get column 1
print(mat[:, 1]) # [2, 4]
```

## Boolean Indexing (Filtering)
Select data based on conditions.
```python
import numpy as np

arr = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40])
mask = arr > 25
print(arr[mask]) # [30, 40]
```
